question: Now that v30 gives a stable reverse gait, is the low speed unlocked by relaxing the stability terms themselves?
gate: 10 s upright on 5 perturbed seeds AND |mean forward speed| >= 0.037 m/s (half the -0.074 command)
method: validate_backward_sustained.py, native MuJoCo, unchanged flat-terrain XML, slew limit on, 3 s warm-up, +/-0.02 qvel perturbations, command -0.074 m/s

full_sweep.note: Every configuration below is a 12M-step PPO run from the v30 checkpoint, 4.1M steps of eval, 1024 envs; only the named weights change.

conclusion: The achieved reverse speed is ~-0.026 m/s under every reward weighting tried, from quadrupling the speed pressure to cutting the stability group to roughly one seventh. All seven configurations are 5/5 stable for the full 10 s. Speed is therefore neither reward-limited nor stability-limited: the fine-tune lands in the same stable reverse gait regardless. This is consistent with the earlier finding that policy tracking of the reference gait, not the reward, is the blocker.

two_attractors.lunge: ~-0.10 m/s then falls at ~1.7 s (v12-v29 family: 0/5)
two_attractors.gap: No reward weighting tried produced an intermediate stable gait; the two behaviours appear to be separate attractors.

status: The stability half of the gate is met (5/5 across every v30-derived candidate). The speed half (>= 0.037 m/s) is not met by any candidate. Nothing promoted, nothing deployed.
next: Short 4.1M-step fine-tunes cannot bridge the gap. Options: (a) far longer training on the stable branch to let the gait lengthen; (b) a contact/foot-placement reference that specifies a longer stride explicitly; (c) a curriculum that moves the command outward from a speed the stable gait already achieves.
